transcript:
Meeting Header:
- Date/Time: 2028-07-19 15:00 PDT
- Duration: ~49 minutes
- Attendees: Ethan Park (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Leah Brooks (Redwood CSM); Carl Voss, Dr. Lena Ortiz, Priya Mehta, Amir Rahman (Peregrine Risk)

Summary:
Quick discovery focused on where Peregrine needs logs and model I/O to live (jurisdictional constraints), and how hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployments map to their audit and encryption requirements. Customer asked for concrete examples of audit evidence and log minimization strategies.

Topics:
- Current infra and data flows
- GDPR/HIPAA overlap and financial regs (MiFID-like internal rules)
- Audit log retention vs redaction requirements
- KMS/HSM integration & key residency
- Network topology for VPC/private control plane
- Tradeoffs: latency, cost, and unit economics of Dedicated vs Private

Transcript Body:
[00:00] Ethan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros, we got about 45, 50 minutes. Maya and I will run through a few questions and then dive into the compliance pieces.
[00:18] Carl: Hey thanks folks, big thing for us is we must keep all customer-identifiable data in EU and in some cases in our UK vaults. we also have internal policies to keep certain logs for seven years, long tail.
[00:35] Maya: Got it, thanks. When you say "logs" can you clarify - are you talking inference request/response bodies, debug logs, or system-level audit trails?
[00:48] Priya: All of the above, really. but we want to make sure PII is either never stored or redacted. our legal team says full request bodies for risk scoring endpoints are considered regulated and must be stored only in eu-resident storage.
[01:12] Dr. Lena: Also HIPAA overlap for our healthcare vertical clients — though Peregrine is primarily financial, some accounts touch health data. We need evidence we can run in a HIPAA posture plus GDPR.
[01:30] Maya: Understood. So three quick vectors: where data persists (residency), who can access logs (RBAC/audit), and key control (KMS/HSM, key residency). Redwood supports Hosted, Dedicated, Private — hosted has region locking for EU but metadata or control plane traces can be in our control plane, so we need to map that to your audit needs.
[01:58] Amir: That's the sticking point. our policy says control plane audit logs need to be within our jurisdiction or accessible with audit procedures. we may require a private control plane if we can't get certs/evidence.
[02:15] Ethan: Right. For Hosted, we provide redacted request logging options and a residency SLO where data at rest can be limited to region X. We also supply exportable audit bundles for SOC2 evidence. for full key residency and private control plane you move to Private (VPC) or on-prem.
[02:43] Carl: Can you talk about log minimization? legal wants minimal stored PII; if we must store tokens for debugging, can that be hashed or tokenized?
[02:57] Maya: Yes, we have redaction hooks at the SDK/proxy layer, you can redact on client side before transmission. also prefix caching (K-V cache) means partial tokens may be cached in memory only; persistent logs can be configured to exclude full request text. note: sometimes transcription captured "K-Vkash" in older notes; ignore that.
[03:25] Priya: How do you handle key management? we use AWS KMS with a strict key policy and don't allow cross-region key usage.
[03:36] Maya: Redwood Private supports BYOK with external KMS and HSM-backed keys; keys never leave your control plane. For Dedicated we can integrate with customer-managed KMS via IAM roles and mTLS, but control plane artifacts may still be in Redwood-managed telemetry unless you request additional isolation.
[04:05] Dr. Lena: For audit, we need the chain-of-custody for model updates and who requested playback of logs. how granular are your audit logs?
[04:18] Leah: We log operator actions, rollout events, who triggered model version switches, and each API auth event with token-level metadata. For Private deployments we can export logs into your SIEM (Splunk/Elastic) with a retention policy you set.
[04:36] Carl: What's the difference in latency between hosted EU region and a Dedicated GPU pool in our own VPC?
[04:50] Maya: Hosted EU region typically sees 30–60ms token latency for standard-medium models; Dedicated on a pinned GPU reduces variance and can be tuned to 20–40ms depending on instance type and batching. Private on-prem is similar to Dedicated but depends on your infra. tradeoff is cost predictability vs marginal latency gain.
[05:20] Amir: Are there fallbacks? if a region goes down can requests failover to another region without violating residency?
[05:29] Ethan: We can do policy-based routing — failover to a different region only if you allow it. if residency is strict, we keep routes in-region and surface capacity errors instead of failing over. we can also do degraded responses to avoid exfil.
[06:00] Priya: Regarding retention, our security team wants a demonstrable delete flow (legal hold exceptions aside). If a customer requests deletion, how do you guarantee removal from caches/backups?
[06:15] Maya: We have deletion APIs that purge persisted logs and mark KV cache entries for GC; for backups we maintain a documented rotation and can provide attestation. In Private installs you control backup policies fully. Hosted will provide deletion logs and a deletion certificate for GDPR audit trails.
[07:02] Carl: There is also a need for cross-border subcontractors — we contract vendor X in US for some analytics. does Redwood allow a mode where only metadata crosses borders for analytics?
[07:17] Ethan: Yes, we can send only aggregated metrics and anonymized telemetry. raw request/response bodies can be prevented from leaving region. that does require configuration and vetting.
[08:23] Lena: We need to map the pieces to our compliance matrix. Can you provide a direct mapping to: data residency, access control, key residency, audit artifacts, retention schedules?
[08:38] Maya: Absolutely. We'll send a mapping doc. Quick question — what's your threshold for requiring private control plane vs Dedicated? is it regulatory requirement or contractual?
[08:54] Carl: A mix. Regulated clients demand private in our SLAs; others we may accept Dedicated with contract clauses. If a client flags it, we need to be able to demonstrate evidence within 48 hours.
[09:10] Priya: On the technical side, requests are routed through our API gateway, then to your inference endpoint. We'll likely run a small NGINX ingress to apply redaction rules; can Redwood support a proxy pattern?
[09:24] Maya: Yes, we support both direct SDK calls and a proxied setup. many customers use a sidecar/proxy to apply PII scrubbing before hitting the inference endpoint. we can also provide middleware snippets in Go/Python.
[10:02] Amir: About encryption in transit — do you support mTLS between our VPC and Redwood Dedicated hosts?
[10:12] Maya: We support mTLS and can provision certs via your PKI or use mutual TLS with client certs you supply. For Private we can do direct peering and private link type connections.
[10:40] Ethan: A few things we've seen in other financials: legal holds, eDiscovery requests, and retention longer than standard. we supply long-term archival hooks to object storage in-region when requested.
[11:05] Carl: If we do a pilot, can you provide a sandbox that simulates our retention and redaction rules?
[11:15] Maya: Yes, our pilot environments let you configure redaction, retention, and KMS options. we can run an ingestion test with sample payloads and show you audit artifacts.
[12:10] Priya: Small nit: earlier notes mentioned "control plane traces may be in Redwood's control plane" can you be explicit what metadata we cannot avoid in Hosted?
[12:25] Leah: On Hosted, control plane events like request routing metrics, model inference latency, and billing metadata are processed in our control plane. We can minimize persisted request text, but some metadata (timestamp, model id, token counts) will be stored for billing/analytics unless you opt for extra contract options.
[12:52] Lena: We will need a legal addendum if we accept Hosted, specifying the boundaries of telemetry and exportability.
[13:05] Ethan: That's normal, we have precedent addenda and can include a clause for telemetry residency and export rights.
[14:00] Carl: About key escrow — in a worst-case legal scenario we might need to hand over decrypted artifacts under court order. do you support split-key or escrow options?
[14:15] Maya: We support BYOK with customer key rotation and can plug into a key escrow workflow. We also support HSM-backed keys where we never have key material. split-key arrangements are possible in Private deployments with your HSM vendor.
[15:30] Priya: Audit sampling — our auditors will want example logs that show an operator deployed a new model, and the timeline of who approved it. do you keep that out of developer-only logs?
[15:45] Leah: Deployment and change logs are part of our operator audit trail and are exportable. they include username, action, timestamp, and model hash. We redact dev-only debug dumps by default from the exported audit bundle.
[16:20] Carl: For billing and token accounting — we need per-tenant token accounting visible in our dashboards. can you provide tenant isolation reports?
[16:33] Ethan: Yes, per-tenant token breakdown, model usage, and cost attribution are standard in Dedicated and Private. Hosted can provide token-level billing but you may need an enterprise plan for long retention.
[17:00] Amir: We also want to ensure our devs can't accidentally send PII to a shared playground. Is there a way to restrict model catalog visibility?
[17:12] Maya: RBAC and model catalog visibility controls exist. You can limit model access by role and by route. we can also lock the catalog to a curated set for your org.
[17:45] Carl: Any known gotchas with prefix caching and GDPR? if prefixes are stored in a cache and later reconstructed, is that a risk?
[17:59] Maya: We treat KV/prefix caches as ephemeral memory; default Hosted caches are in-memory and TTL-limited. for strict GDPR needs we can disable caching or use ephemeral-only caches that are not persisted. we can also add additional scrubbing to the cache pipeline.
[18:30] Priya: For your PKI integration, how long does it take to set up mTLS with our CA?
[18:40] Maya: Usually 3–7 business days for certificate exchange and validation, assuming network peering reqs are straightforward. complex firewall setups add time.
[19:10] Ethan: Quick commercial question — does Peregrine prefer committed capacity (Dedicated) or pay-as-you-go (Hosted) for pilot?
[19:22] Carl: We prefer pay-as-you-go for the pilot but need the option to move to Dedicated fast if a regulated client requires it. also budget needs sign-off by the 31st of July.
[19:37] Lena: we'll need a clear runbook of evidence to give auditors within 48 hours for either mode.
[19:48] Maya: We'll provide a runbook template and example evidence set. It includes logs export, deletion certificates, key rotation records, and model change artifacts.
[20:30] Carl: On data residency for backups — you said we can have object storage snapshots in-region. how about cold archives? sometimes those go to a different cloud region.
[20:43] Leah: We can policy-mark archive snapshots to remain in-region; you'll have to accept possible cost delta. we document archive locations for audits.
[21:10] Priya: Are there monitoring hooks so our security ops can detect anomalous calls or potential leak patterns?
[21:22] Maya: Yes, we publish tracing hooks and webhooks for anomaly alerts; you can connect to your SIEM and trigger automated workflows.
[22:00] Amir: Competitor check - we looked at a competitor that claimed full in-region control plane. is that solved by Private?
[22:12] Ethan: Yes, Private gives you a private control plane option. but note the ops responsibility increases; Redwood can run it as a managed offering or hand off fully to your infra team depending on the contract.
[22:45] Carl: SLA expectations — if we move to Dedicated with reserved capacity, what are the latency/uptime guarantees?
[22:57] Maya: We offer SLA-backed uptime tiers for Dedicated and Private with response time targets, and escalation paths. we'll include the specific SLO numbers in the proposal.
[23:30] Priya: Ok, practical test plan for pilot — we'll send sample payloads, you run them to the sandbox with our redaction rules and show audit exports.
[23:45] Maya: Great. We'll also run a small benchmark to show token latency and give a cost estimate for the expected QPS.
[24:05] Lena: On the legal side, we'll need to see example contractual language for telemetry boundaries and a sample addendum for control plane residency.
[24:18] Ethan: We'll share a template NDA/Amendment and the telemetry addendum.
[25:00] Carl: Anything else — network peering costs? sometimes cloud providers charge for cross-region traffic.
[25:10] Ethan: Yes, those egress charges are typically passed through; we'll call that out in the pricing worksheet.
[25:45] Priya: The only remaining question is whether Redwood's hosted telemetry could contain query identifiers that map back to user IDs. we need assurances that any identifiers are pseudonymized.
[26:00] Leah: We can pseudonymize identifiers, and provide mapping artifacts only if you request them under a legal process. default is pseudonymization for aggregated telemetry.
[26:30] Maya: quick note: some transcripts or auto-captions can mangle product names (we saw "K-Vkash" earlier). the system is good but not perfect; just a heads up for auditors if they look at auto transcripts.
[27:05] Carl: Fair. for the follow-up deep dive — we'll include our infra lead and one of our auditors. timing wise next Wed afternoon is best.
[27:20] Ethan: We'll send a calendar invite after the call.
[28:00] (discussion continues through implementation specifics and scheduling)
[40:12] Maya: Recap: we'll send three artifacts — decision checklist (hosted vs dedicated vs private), SOC2/ISO/KMS integration guide, and a pilot test plan with sample payload instructions.
[40:30] Carl: Good. if we decide to pilot Hosted with strict telemetry redaction, legal will review the addendum and either accept or push for Dedicated/Private.
[41:05] Leah: We'll include example audit bundles so your auditors can triage quickly.
[42:22] Priya: We'll gather sample payloads and a redaction spec; expect that by Friday.
[43:00] Ethan: Perfect. final note, we'll include cost estimates for both pay-as-you-go and a 12-month committed Dedicated plan so you can compare unit economics.
[43:22] Carl: Thanks everyone.
[43:40] Dr. Lena: Thank you, looking forward to the mapping doc.
[44:00] Ethan: We'll follow up within two business days. thanks all.
